title: Thuế carbon và hộ thu nhập thấp · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support taxing household carbon emissions more heavily, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

outline.purpose: Dạng discuss yêu cầu giải thích riêng vì sao mỗi phía tin lập trường của mình rồi đưa phán đoán của người viết. Trong bài này, cân nhắc trọng tâm là: Giá carbon đưa một phần thiệt hại môi trường vào chi phí lựa chọn. Người có xe buýt thay thế mới dễ đổi hành vi; giá cao tạo động lực nhưng không tự tạo phương án đi lại. Người ít khả năng thay đổi có thể trả nhiều hơn mà không giảm phát thải. Hoàn tiền giảm gánh nặng thu nhập; đầu tư phương án sạch tăng khả năng đổi hành vi. Hai biện pháp xử lý hai phần khác nhau của phản biện.
outline.content: Supporters argue that carbon pricing can discourage wasteful energy use. Opponents respond that poorer households may have little control over inefficient rented homes or long commuting distances. I favour higher carbon charges where households can realistically change consumption, while accepting opponents' demand for protection when renting, income or location makes cleaner choices inaccessible.

paragraphs: Supporters argue that carbon pricing can discourage wasteful energy use. Opponents respond that poorer households may have little control over inefficient rented homes or long commuting distances. I favour higher carbon charges where households can realistically change consumption, while accepting opponents' demand for protection when renting, income or location makes cleaner choices inaccessible.

Carbon pricing can discourage wasteful energy use. When environmental damage enters the price of a journey or a product, consumers have a reason to consider cleaner alternatives. A household with access to frequent buses might replace some short car journeys. Price incentives are more credible when changing behaviour is practical; without that possibility, the charge operates mainly as an additional household expense. A higher price can change travel choices where alternatives exist, but it cannot enable a tenant to insulate a property that the landlord controls.

Poorer households may have little control over inefficient rented homes or long commuting distances. A household may face a higher energy bill without having authority to improve its rented property or access to a usable transport alternative. In that situation, the tax reduces disposable income more readily than it reduces emissions. Revenue should fund targeted rebates and realistic low-carbon alternatives. Rebates address immediate affordability, whereas better transport and housing efficiency expand the choices available; neither function should be mistaken for the other. The policy should be judged by emissions reductions and household affordability together, with particular attention to people unable to change their energy use.

The environmental argument supports pricing emissions, while the fairness argument requires rebates and usable alternatives; combining them is stronger than expecting financial pressure alone to change consumption that households cannot avoid.

paragraphs.quote: Poorer households may have little control over inefficient rented homes or long commuting distances. A household may face a higher energy bill without having authority to improve its rented property or access to a usable transport alternative. In that situation, the tax reduces disposable income more readily than it reduces emissions. Revenue should fund targeted rebates and realistic low-carbon alternatives.
